## v2.9 Platform Completion (executed 2026-02-20 → 2026-02-23, never archived)

| Phase | Name | Goal | Plans | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 80 | Richer Negotiation | Agents negotiate delegation scope through counter-proposals and resolve ambiguity through mid-task clarification, replacing the binary accept/reject handshake | 5 | passed (21/21 must-haves verified) |
| 81 | Parallel Delegation | Orchestrator agents can fan out work to multiple delegates simultaneously with policy-driven completion semantics | 6 | passed (5/5 must-haves verified) |
| 82 | Transparent Materialization | Delegated tasks can optionally create corresponding Linear tickets, giving human operators visibility into agent-to-agent work through their existing tools | 5 | passed (12/12 must-haves verified) |
| 83 | Tree-Level Token Budgets | Token spending across an entire delegation tree is tracked and enforced as a single budget, preventing runaway costs from parallel or deep delegation chains | 4 | passed (16/16 must-haves verified) |
| 84 | Scheduled Execution | Agents can run on a schedule for periodic work like backlog grooming or monitoring, breaking the purely reactive event-driven model | 3 | passed (12/12 must-haves verified) |
| 85 | Sub-Agent Discovery (deferred) | Orchestrator agents select sub-agents by describing the capability they need, replacing hardcoded agent ID references in spawn calls | 0 | — |
| 86 | Persistent Agent Identity | Agents accumulate understanding across conversations through structured identity documents, and the framework provides a lifecycle hook mechanism for injecting turns at conversation boundaries | 3 | passed (5/5 must-haves verified) |
| 87 | Knowledge Retrieval Enhancement | The knowledge retrieval pipeline is pluggable for future strategies, and agents get a chance to persist important knowledge before history compaction discards it | 3 | passed (4/4 success criteria verified) |
